title: Lena S
content: I was diagnosed with stage four cancer when I was age of 26, in 2006. I had chemotherapy, radiation, and a radical hysterectomy. After my third round of chemo, I got very sick and started vomiting for the first time during my treatment. I went to the emergency room and was kept there for eight hours as they tried to bring my fever down while I continued to vomit. The nurse on staff kept me there because she knew this was not a normal symptom for me. She insisted the doctor order a blood culture. After eight hours they sent me home. The results of the blood culture should not have come back for 48 hours, but the next morning they called and told me I had an infection. I went back to the hospital. As I entered my room, I told my nurse that my heart had started to hurt. They laid me down on the bed and put a blood pressure cuff on me. I looked to my left and saw that my blood pressure was 40/20 before I blacked out. The first image I had was of me being on a bus with no seats in the middle. The bus seemed to be going very fast with trees and other things flying past the window. I looked to my left and saw my grandfather sitting at the back. He had passed away five years earlier. He was wearing the clothes he typically wore, holding his cane, and looking out the window. Then everything went black again as I went unconscious. The next vision I had was the same thing with a bus going fast and trees flying by. To my left, at the end of the bus, was my grandfather again. He was still holding his cane and looking out the window. But this time, he was wearing hospital clothes. The vision went black again. When I woke up, there were a number of doctors and nurses standing around me in the intensive care unit (ICU). I remember waking up from that vision, thinking that it felt like the best nap I had ever taken. When I saw the nurses and doctors over me, I felt so much at peace. I said, "Hello, everyone." The sepsis was so severe that they had to put me on a ventilator, and they did not think I would make it through the night.

elements.At the time of your experience, was ther: Yes, Illness, Ventilator, Life threatening event, but not clinical death
elements.How did your highest level of consciousn: More consciousness and alertness than normal, I was kind of foggy from the chemo and drugs, and I was not feeling well. When I woke up from that vision, everything felt clear.
elements.Did time seem to speed up or slow down?: Time seemed to go faster or slower than usual, It seemed like we were going really fast.
elements.Please compare your vision during the ex: I was not feeling well prior to my vision. When I woke up from having the vision, I felt very at peace and comfortable for a little while.
elements.Did you pass into or through a tunnel?: Yes, It felt like I was on a bus passing by trees, but headed somewhere.
elements.Did you seem to enter some other, uneart: Some unfamiliar and strange place, It felt like I was heading out of earth and going somewhere.
elements.What emotions did you feel during the ex: I felt very at peace and calm.
elements.Did you feel a sense of harmony or unity: I felt united or one with the world
elements.Did you come to a border or point of no: I came to a barrier that I was not permitted to cross; or was sent back against my will, I felt like my grandfather in hospital clothes was sending me back to earth and saying it was not my time.
elements.Did your experience include features con: Content that was entirely consistent with the beliefs you had at the time of your experience
elements.Did you have a change in your values and: Yes, I truly believed that there was a heaven and that our family and friends are waiting for us.
elements.During your experience, did you gain spe: Yes, I felt like my grandfather was telling me that my time was not up and I needed to continue doing work down on earth.
elements.During your experience, did you gain inf: Yes, I felt like my grandfather showed me that he was the guide that was supposed to take me to another place.
elements.How accurately do you remember the exper: I remember the experience more accurately than other life events that occurred around the time of the experience
